claims.claim: A warmed-up Spring MVC endpoint that parses a small JSON body and does one insert uses roughly 0.5–1 ms of CPU per request
claims.measured: java-spring: 7,668 req/s at 100% CPU for one Postgres row (~0.13 ms CPU/request); java-spring-vt: 12,731 req/s at 99% (~0.08 ms); JSON: 27,264 req/s at 98% (~0.04 ms)
claims.why: One measured query costs about 0.08–0.13 ms of CPU, so 0.5–1 ms is roughly 4–12 times too high.

claims.claim: At 200 requests a second that's about 20–30% CPU at peak
claims.measured: 200 / 7,668 req/s ≈ 2.6% of one core (java-spring); 200 / 12,731 ≈ 1.6% (java-spring-vt), single-row DB test
claims.why: The measurements suggest about 2–3% CPU at 200 req/s, nearly 10 times less than claimed.

claims.claim: The real limits are memory and the database, not Java's speed
claims.measured: java-spring 7,668 req/s and java-spring-vt 12,731 req/s on the single-row DB test, against a 200/s need; peak memory 307–499 MB in a 512 MB container
claims.why: Throughput is far above the need while peak memory comes close to 512 MB, so memory is the tighter limit.

claims.claim: A lean Spring Boot app (web, JDBC, actuator) typically uses about 200–300 MB of memory
claims.measured: java-spring peak 220 MB (plaintext), 312 MB (JSON), 499 MB (DB); java-spring-vt 209–444 MB; idle 131–134 MB
claims.why: Measured peaks of 209–499 MB are all within a factor of 2 of the 200–300 MB range.

claims.claim: Go is technically the easiest fit for 512 MB (about 30 MB of memory)
claims.measured: go-gin peak 8–16 MB (12 MB on DB), go-nethttp 7–15 MB (11 MB on DB); idle 2 MB
claims.why: The direction is right, but measured Go memory is 7–16 MB (11–12 MB on the DB test), so 30 MB overstates it by more than 2 times for the relevant workload.

claims.measured: go-gin 293 ms, go-nethttp 238 ms vs java-spring 5,939 ms
claims.why: Go starts in under 0.3 s, about 20 times faster than Spring Boot.

claims.claim: Python is also slow on 1 vCPU
claims.measured: DB single row: python-fastapi 3,706, flask 1,529–2,119 req/s vs java-spring 7,668 and java-spring-vt 12,731; fib: Python 1,047–1,257 vs java-spring 14,258
claims.why: The Python servers measured several times slower than Spring Boot on every test.

claims.claim: Slow startup on 1 vCPU (roughly 10–20 seconds plus JIT warm-up)
claims.measured: java-spring 5,939 ms, java-spring-vt 6,224 ms start-up on 1 CPU
claims.why: Measured start-up was about 6 s, so 10–20 s is 1.7–3.4 times too high, and most of that range is more than 2 times too high.

claims.claim: Quarkus or Micronaut have lower memory and are built for small machines
GraalVM native image cuts memory to about 100 MB and starts instantly
JPA/Hibernate uses more memory than plain SQL
claims.why: The measurements don't compare data-access layers.

claims.claim: Spring's class-data-sharing / AOT cache speeds up startup
claims.why: Start-up was measured only for one configuration, without a CDS/AOT comparison.
